newsitem.title: USA: Pennzoil buys Brooklyn Union stake in unit.
newsitem.headline: Pennzoil buys Brooklyn Union stake in unit.

text.p: Pennzoil Co said Friday it has acquired Brooklyn Union Gas Co's 50 percent ownership interest in PennUnion Energy Services LLC, a natural gas marketing firm based in Houston.
Terms of the sale were not disclosed.

PennUnion began as a joint venture between the two companies' subsidiaries, Pennzoil Gas Marketing Co and BRING Gas Services Corp, in April 1995. Each company owned 50 percent of the venture, Pennzoil said.
"PennUnion is now well established," said James L. Pate, Pennzoil's chief executive officer.
"Pennzoil is acquiring Brooklyn Union's interest in the joint venture in order to pursue natural gas marketing opportunities nationwide," he said.
PennUnion markets some 1.4 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day, including all of Pennzoil's domestic production, which represents more than half of PennUnion's sales.

Brooklyn Union chief executive Robert B. Catell said, "We have sold our interest in PennUnion because we wanted to focus our efforts on the retail market through our newly formed and wholly-owned subsidiary, KeySpan Energy Services Inc. Earlier this year, we formed KeySpan Energy Services to take advantage of local unbundling in the Northeast. Later this year, we plan to launch an energy services business to meet the needs of large customers in the region."
